newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria Pfizer buys out foreign partners.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria Pfizer buys out foreign partners.

text.p: Shareholders of Pfizer Products Nigeria Plc on Tuesday approved a management buy-out of the company from its divesting foreign technical partners.
They also adopted a new name for the company.
Both decisions were approved at its annual general meeting in Lagos.

"Following the decision of Pfizer Corporation of the U.S. to divest from the company, management acquired 51 percent of its 60 percent equity holding and disposed of the remaining nine percent on the floor of the Nigerian stock exchange," its chief executive, Sam Ohuabunwa, said.
He said the firm executed the management buy-out through the formation of Worldwide Healthcare Ltd. which would warehouse the shares for members of staff and management.
The company was also renamed Neimeth International Pharmaceuticals Plc.
Ohuabunwa said the development meant a better future for the workforce.
Under the new arrangement, Neimeth would remain the exclusive agent for Pfizer's products in Nigeria and would be free to expand its range of products.
Analysts and shareholders welcomed the management buy-out, saying it afforded the Nigerians an opportunity to make the company the country's foremost pharmaceutical firm.
"If well managed, it should be one of the key leaders in this market," said Alex Osunde of Enterprise Stockbrokers.
The company's profit after tax in the year ended November 1996 fell to 31.9 million naira from 58.4 million in 1995.
Pfizer shares closed steady at 7.30 naira on the Nigerian stock market on Tuesday.
